clue.text: Eat rice, get convoluted modern device

indicators.note: something convoluted is twisted up, so the preceding words are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters of these three words, used as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is told to eat rice and is then handed a gadget that is too complicated to use.
explanation.definitionFit: The electronic cigarette, or vape, is a recent invention, a battery-powered gadget that vaporises nicotine liquid.

clue.text: Observe onset of flipping apocalypse

indicators.note: flipping turns the following word back to front before anything is taken
onset means the start, so only the opening letters of the flipped word are kept

parts.note: the last four letters of the word, which become the opening four once it is turned round

explanation.surface: A watcher sees the first signs of the end of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned round, apocalypse begins ESPY..., and its onset is those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or notice something, a literary synonym for observing.

clue.text: Part of bike, aluminium chain

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a piece lying inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the end of bike and the start of aluminium

explanation.surface: A bicycle component: a chain made of aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: Chain looks like the bike part, but it means a chain of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish furniture retailer operates a worldwide group of stores, which is a retail chain.

clue.text: Play with plaything?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Ibsen's famous drama of 1879
second meaning: a miniature toy home for dolls

explanation.walkthrough: Play looks like a verb inviting you to have fun with a toy; it is a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen wrote a celebrated drama of this title, and the same phrase names a child's miniature toy home.

clue.text: Shown European, persuaded Tory to leave

parts.note: standard abbreviation for European

indicators.note: to leave tells us those letters must go out of the word they sit in

parts.note: a synonym for persuaded
Con is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: A political story: a European was shown something and talked a Conservative into quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is the usual short form for a Conservative, and Tory is the nickname for one, so the party label is what departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to display or make evident a feeling or quality, so evinced means displayed.

clue.text: Take trick before east voided and boast

parts.note: in card games, to trump is to take a trick with a trump card

indicators.note: voided means emptied, so the inside of the word goes and only its outside letters stay

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A card player wins a trick, leads from the empty east hand, and crows about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Before places TRUMP ahead of the emptied east.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim it loudly, a verb for bragging about it.

clue.text: Revolutionary plans to send annoying messages

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the following word is read backwards

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Radicals scheme to send bothersome messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To spam is to flood people with unwanted emails or texts, a verb from the junk-mail sense.

clue.text: Quiet deceiver concealing silver: is master revealing theft?

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a liar deceives
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: A quiet crook hides the silver, and a schoolmaster asks whether this exposes a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: Quiet gives p from piano, the musical direction to play softly; the silver is tucked in just after the deceiver's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarism is the stealing of another person's words or ideas and passing them off as one's own.

clue.text: Hot old oven on cliff somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit before the later one

parts.note: hot under the collar, furious
an Aga is a traditional cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of old British kitchens
a scar is a steep rocky cliff face

explanation.surface: An old oven left out on a clifftop in the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island nation lies off Africa's south-east coast, so it is a place in that continent.

clue.text: Advanced highly rated holding company

indicators.note: holding means having something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: precious means valued highly
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A well-regarded firm with a stake in another business.
explanation.walkthrough: Advanced looks like a verb about the firm; here it is an adjective for a child ahead of their years.
explanation.definitionFit: A precocious child is advanced for their age, developing abilities earlier than usual.

clue.text: Measure that's used to exercise prisoners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a unit of length of three feet
second meaning: the enclosed area of a jail where inmates walk

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an imperial unit of length and an enclosed open space, such as a prison exercise ground.

clue.text: Dish, bland, pig and duck purée

indicators.note: a purée is food mashed to a pulp, so the words before it are pulped and remixed

parts.note: taken as written for the fodder
taken as written for the fodder
taken as written for the fodder

explanation.surface: A menu item: a dull mash of pork and duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Black pudding is a British blood sausage made with pork fat and oats.
explanation.definitionFit: This blood sausage is a traditional item served at a cooked British breakfast, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Somewhere in Africa, challenges Everyman to leave meat containing hint of aniseed

parts.note: to dare someone is to challenge them

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the shortened meat
to leave tells us the setter's letter must go out of the word for meat

parts.note: salami is a cured sausage meat
the setter refers to himself, which in wordplay gives I

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A setter is dared to go off and eat meat flavoured with aniseed somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: SALAMI loses its I to become SALAM, which then holds the A: SALA(A)M.
explanation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is Tanzania's largest city and chief port on the East African coast.

clue.text: Large creature and small creature's whitish, says Spooner

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: worm is a small creature and pale is whitish; with the possessive s attached to pale, swap the W and SP sounds

explanation.surface: A big beast and a tiny pale one, described by a famously tongue-tied clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, worm's pale runs as worm spale; Spooner swaps the opening W and SP.
explanation.definitionFit: This toothed whale is the largest predator alive, so it is a very big animal.

clue.text: Tailored dean's suits by yourself

indicators.note: tailored clothes are cut and refashioned, so the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters, apostrophe dropped, used as the fodder

explanation.surface: A college dean's suits were made to measure, and he dressed himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unassisted means doing it alone, without help from anyone else.

clue.text: Thin stole

definitions.meaning: second meaning: took without permission, in informal speech

explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like a noun, the fur wrap, beside the thin; it is the past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinched face looks gaunt and drawn, and to pinch something is slang for stealing it.

clue.text: Restroom mostly refreshed for Spanish performers

indicators.note: something refreshed is made over anew, so the remaining letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before shortening

explanation.surface: A washroom is mostly freshened up ready for visiting Spanish entertainers.
explanation.definitionFit: Toreros are bullfighters, who perform in the bullring in front of a crowd in Spain.

clue.text: Saves, regrets holding keyboard key

indicators.note: holding means having something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone saves a file, then regrets having pressed a key.
explanation.walkthrough: Saves suggests saving a computer file, which suits the keyboard; here it means pulling someone out of danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from danger, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Dash hurriedly with temperature dropping, dash to and fro

indicators.note: as a temperature drops, one temperature letter gives way to the other in the word

parts.note: to scuttle is to run with short hurried steps

explanation.surface: Someone rushes about as the weather turns cold, darting back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: C (cold) and H (hot) are the letters on taps; one is swapped for the other in SCUTTLE. The swap runs from C to H, so the clue's dropping is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuttle is to travel back and forth repeatedly between two places, like a loom shuttle.

clue.text: Primarily, remote oceanic section, some skirting East Antarctica?

definitions.text: remote oceanic section, some skirting East Antarctica

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

parts.words: remote oceanic section, some skirting East Antarctica
parts.note: the initial letters of the seven words

explanation.surface: A geography note on a far-flung stretch of ocean along the Antarctic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition; the question mark admits the Ross Sea actually lies more off West Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean cutting into the Antarctic coastline, a remote polar waterway.

clue.text: One standing on leaf? Tea leaf?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsical: someone who treads on dry leaves makes them crackle and rustle
second meaning: tea leaf is Cockney rhyming slang for thief, and this is a thief of livestock

explanation.walkthrough: Tea leaf is London rhyming slang for a thief; the answer is someone who steals cattle or horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a whimsical noun for whoever makes leaves crackle and a cattle thief, a slang thief.

clue.text: Nicholas II's preferred way to serve vodka?

definitions.text: Nicholas II's preferred way to serve vodka?

parts.note: the setter's reading: the last tsar's side in the civil war was the Whites, against the Bolshevik Reds
the surface reading: a cocktail of vodka, coffee liqueur and cream

explanation.surface: A question about how the last Tsar of Russia liked his vodka.
explanation.walkthrough: The anti-Bolshevik Whites fought for the old order Nicholas II stood for, so he would favour them.
explanation.definitionFit: This vodka cocktail with coffee liqueur and cream shares its name with the counter-revolutionary loyalists.

clue.text: A month in Spain (and part of Ireland)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Spanish name for the fifth month
second meaning: a county on Ireland's west coast

explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed second half reads like an aside to a holiday, but it is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for the fifth calendar month is also the name of a western Irish county.

clue.text: Kelly's inheritance?

parts.note: the surface reading: something left to a person named Kelly in a will
the setter's reading: the first name of the dancer of Singin' in the Rain, which is also a unit of heredity

explanation.surface: A question about what someone called Kelly was left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first name of the Hollywood dancer Kelly and also the biological unit passing traits from parents.

clue.text: Voice in maëlstrom regularly lost

indicators.note: losing letters at regular intervals means every other letter goes, the rest kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A singer's voice is drowned out in the whirl of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singing voice, the lowest female range or a high male one, between soprano and tenor.

clue.text: Styled á la Titian etc, for starters?

indicators.note: to style something is to arrange it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the fodder
taken as written for the fodder

indicators.note: starters are the opening course, so only the first letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the abbreviation

explanation.surface: An art-history remark about work done in the manner of Titian and his kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Italianate means in an Italian manner, as work modelled on a Venetian Renaissance master would be.

clue.text: Maëlstrom's exciting in East End

indicators.note: London's East End is Cockney country, where the initial H of a spoken word is dropped

parts.note: heady means exciting; spoken without its H it is the answer

explanation.surface: A dramatic whirlpool is called thrilling in a London accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, from the East End of London, famously drops initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of water, a small-scale whirlpool, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Sculptor's King And His Victim Eating Duck

parts.note: Henry, one of several English kings, here Henry VIII

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Thomas More was executed on Henry VIII's orders in 1535
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A headline-style claim that a sculptor's king and his victim are eating duck.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside MORE after MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Moore was the English artist famed for large bronze reclining figures, a leading modern sculptor.
